target_customer: Home services companies such as roofing contractors whose reps run in-home sales appointments
problem: In-home sales reps get little coaching or follow-up support and spend time on CRM entry, while managers cannot see which reps need help.
business_model: Outcome-based pricing, a flat fee per sold project
product_category: AI sales assistant for field and in-home sales

founders.name: David Tondreau
founders.background_notes: YC page says manufacturing engineer at Rolls-Royce, five years at Dexterity ending as senior manager, 15 patents. His bio calls him CEO of Maive, relationship to Ladder unclear.

founders.name: Will Cray
education: Pursuing Master's in Machine Learning, UT Austin (completion not stated)
previous_startups: Own computer vision and machine learning startup (name and outcome not given)
founders.background_notes: ML and computer vision tech lead at Dexterity per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Recording and transcribing in-person conversations plus coaching, CRM sync and integrations with ServiceTitan and AccuLynx is standard LLM application engineering with noisy audio as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: CRM integrations and conversation data from reps give some stickiness, but conversation AI is easy to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. The product depends on ServiceTitan and AccuLynx integrations, which could be copied by the platforms.

market_need_then: Home services firms run large volumes of in-home sales; the company claims about $106 million in sold projects handled, a self-reported figure on its site.

branding.domain_note: Uses ladderai.com, not ladder.com, as of 2025. Many other companies are named Ladder.

identity.logo: Green logo lockup per the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Short confident fragments such as Give your reps an assistant, not a supervisor

branding.brand_signature: Elevate your reps / an assistant, not a supervisor positioning

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared by several other Ladder companies, and no press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Ladder is a Winter 2025 company with two founders from robotics and computer vision and no reported exit or shutdown. Its flat per-sold-project pricing and early customer logos suggest some traction, but no verified funding or revenue was found. The name is generic and shared with other firms, which could hurt search discoverability.
notes: Competitor search for the batch period returned only generic home services AI tool roundups with no dated entry I could cite, so the list is empty. Funding search found nothing for this company; results were other companies named Ladder. Do not confuse with Ladder (construction labor, acquired by Buildforce). No outcome news found.
